\section{Overview}
\subsection*{Brief: pd-trigger-lite}
Owner's words: "a simple pd trigger board like the showcase one ... No need to copy the existing ... Ideally low cost ... the zips and component placement files so I can order PCB cheaply from JLC".

Design intent (set by the dispatching planning session; unattended run - the owner is away, every recipe question is decided here and recorded with state.py decision):

\begin{itemize}
\item USB-C PD SINK trigger, 2-layer, 1 oz, small (aim \textless{}= \textasciitilde{}25 x 15 mm; bigger only if DRC needs it).
\item CH224K (LCSC C970725) with its minimal application circuit.
\item Voltage selectable after assembly with no tool beyond a soldering iron (solder jumpers /
0R links), sensible assembled default 12 V.
\item Output: VBUS + GND on two large 2.54 mm-compatible through-hole pads, no screw terminal.
Rated 3 A (no e-marker, so 3 A is the cable/source ceiling).
\item One power LED if it costs one basic resistor + one basic LED.
\item A bulk/input cap per datasheet. No TVS/fuse unless the datasheet requires it.
\item JLC BASIC parts everywhere possible; USB-C connector and CH224K are extended - cheapest
widely stocked power-only receptacle exposing CC1/CC2.
\item Deliverables: gerber zip, JLC BOM.csv + CPL.csv, order quote for qty 5 with assembly,
owner guide PDF, README. Never place an order.
\item Showcase boards/pd-trigger: learn from it, reuse its CH224K extraction, do not copy its
layout or feature set.
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Variant brief: pd-trigger-lite-dip (2026-09-24)}
Planning session: copy pd-trigger-lite, replace the voltage-select 0603 links with an SMD DIP switch so the output voltage is chosen by switch, with 5 V as one choice. CH224A, 5-position switch one-hot: pos1 CFG1 -\textgreater{} 100k -\textgreater{} VHV (5 V), pos2-5 CFG1 -\textgreater{} 6.8k/24k/56k/120k -\textgreater{} GND. Grow the board only as needed. Same deliverables as lite. No order, no spend.

\section{Requirements}
\subsection*{Requirements: pd-trigger-lite-dip}
Variant of pd-trigger-lite: the solder links are replaced by a 5-position DIP switch (5 V added).

Source: \texttt{brief/brief.md}. Written inline by the orchestrator (no requirements-analyst spawn: a one-block board, recorded as a decision). Unattended run: every open item below was answered by the orchestrator as the owner's delegate and recorded with \texttt{state.py decision}. Mode: none (the brief carries no mode token) - design normally.

\subsubsection*{1. Function}
A low-cost USB-C Power Delivery trigger. A PD sink controller negotiates a fixed voltage from a USB-C PD charger and passes VBUS straight through to two output pads. No regulation, no conversion, no switching element in the power path. The requested voltage is chosen by a 5-position DIP switch: 5, 9, 12, 15 or 20 V.

\subsubsection*{2. Interfaces}
\begin{itemize}
\item Input: USB-C receptacle, power-only use, PD SINK. CC1/CC2 to the controller; D+/D- to
the controller's DP/DM per the datasheet reference (no USB data function).
\item Output: VBUS and GND on two 2.54 mm-pitch plated through-holes (take a 1x2 header or
wires). No screw terminal (cost).
\item Voltage selection: SW1, one switch per voltage (5/9/12/15/20 V), exactly one ON, set
before plugging in. All assembled at JLC; the switch is an extended part.
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{3. Power}
\begin{itemize}
\item Input: USB-C PD source, 5 V default, negotiated 9/12/15/20 V.
\item Output current rating: 3 A continuous at any voltage (a non-e-marked cable caps the
contract at 3 A; the board makes no 5 A claim).
\item Controller supply: from VBUS directly (CH224A VHV pin is rated 32 V).
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{4. Environment}
Bench use, indoor, 0-50 C ambient. No enclosure, no battery, no mains.

\subsubsection*{5. Size \& mounting}
Target \textless{}= 25 x 15 mm (soft; grow only if DRC needs it). No mounting holes (cost/size; the board hangs off its cable and output wires).

\subsubsection*{6. Quantity \& budget}
Quantity 5, JLCPCB PCB + economy PCBA, lowest cost. JLC Basic parts wherever possible.

\subsubsection*{7. Assembly}
Single-sided SMT at JLC. The 1x2 output header is optional and hand-fitted by the owner.

\subsubsection*{8. Compliance/safety flags}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textgreater{}3 A: NO (3 A max). Mains: NO. Battery: NO.
\item Protection: no TVS/fuse - the controller datasheet requires none (decision recorded).
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{9. Open questions}
None open. Every question was answered by the orchestrator as delegate (see state.json decisions): controller part, selection method, default voltage, output format, current rating, LED, bulk cap, protection.
